verdict: Two libraries share this folder. Six newer guides (youth-who-am-i, forty-days, when-our-parents-grow-old, divorce-and-blended-families, waiting-for-the-light, addiction-and-recovery) are in the mature register: contractions, paragraphs, Scripture quoted with its reference, no third-person 'Bell', help lines present. The other sixty-two were built from one template and read as machine-made in bulk: a narrator describing 'Bell' inside his own teaching (1,873 times), the editorial rulebook written into the prose (steelman, verdict, indictment, 'this platform'), his biography stamped as a credential on 49 guides, 'It is not X. It is Y.' about 1,850 times, 'honest' about 3,350 times, zero contractions, and every teaching one unbroken paragraph of 750 to 1,570 words. Mechanically the library is clean: no em-dashes, no exclamation points outside Scripture, no live Forbidden Language beyond 'the blessed life'.

what_was_read.note: The brief asked for twenty guides read in full. Each guide is 20,000 to 28,000 words (the folder is about 1.6 million words), so twenty in full was more than one pass could hold. One guide was read end to end; for the other twenty-nine I read the summary, leader primer, one full or head-and-tail teaching, case study, going-deeper, an objection, the facilitator script and the promo kit. All 68 were scanned by script for every pattern below, and the counts are from all 68.

pattern_counts.third-person Bell: 1,873 uses, all 68 files; 118 of ~340 teaching fields
pattern_counts.biography stamp (atheism / no father / f: 297 mentions in 49 guides; 71 in FAQ answers, 60 in summaries, 45 in leader primers, 31 in facilitator openings, 38 in promo copy
pattern_counts.rulebook words (steelman, verdict, indic: about 950; verdict 485, at full strength 161, steelman 80, inside the indictment 66
pattern_counts.\"is not X. It is Y.\": about 1,858 (27 per guide); 309 of 549 quote cards are built on a negation contrast
pattern_counts.exclamation points outside Scripture: 0 (86 found, all in quoted Scripture or memory verses)
pattern_counts.forbidden words: 0 live ("authenticate" and "journeyed" are different words or Scripture; "the blessed life" 4 times outside the Beatitudes guide)

most_his: fatherhood (first person, paragraphed, but no contractions and "So here is the verdict")
library_wide_rules_for_the_fixer: Never 'Bell' inside summary, teaching, objections, FAQ or scripts. In teaching, James speaks as 'I' or 'we'. In leader notes, say 'the study' or 'this session', or just say the thing.

Keep the biography in at most one place per guide (the one teaching where it bears on the subject, e.g. fatherhood session 1, prayer session 1), in his own first person, one plain sentence. Delete it from summaries, primers, FAQ, facilitator openings and all promo copy.

Delete every use of steelman/steel-man, 'inside the indictment', 'self-implication', 'even-handedness', 'this platform', 'the method is the message/mercy', and 'verdict' used of the study's own conclusion. Do the fair thing; don't name it.
Cut announced turns: 'Then the turn.', 'Then the reversal.', 'This is the hinge.', 'Grant all of it.', 'But here is what the objection misses', 'Now the verdict...'. Say the next thing.
Leave one 'not X, it is Y' per session at the real hinge; turn the rest into plain positive statements. Rebuild quote cards so most are not antithesis pairs.
Add contractions wherever the line is spoken or addressed to 'you' (facilitator script first, then teaching). Leave Scripture and prayers alone.
Break each teaching into paragraphs of roughly 100 to 160 words at its existing turns. Do not reorder.

Vary or drop the shared stamps ('Come honest, not finished.', 'Every question carries the answer behind it...', 'No, and the study is careful here.', 'It will not do that, and the leader must never let it.').
Verify each bibliography entry, then delete every 'Leader to confirm...' note.
Use the six newer guides as the model for all of the above.

ten_worst.quote: Now let me do the thing this platform requires, which is to state each position in its strongest form, the form its own best defenders would sign, so that you cannot tell from the steelman alone where I land.
ten_worst.why: This is the editorial standard pasted into a pastor's mouth: 'this platform', 'steelman', 'the form its own defenders would sign'. No one talks to a small group this way.
ten_worst.replacement: Let me state each position the way its best defenders would.
ten_worst.pattern: P3 rulebook leakage (the prose describing its own method)

ten_worst.quote: I want to state both cases so honestly that you could not tell, from the steelman alone, where I land, and only then will I tell you, and only then will I tell you why it matters far less for our fellowship than the volume of the argument would suggest.
ten_worst.tell: Rulebook leakage; 'honestly' self-certifying; doubled 'and only then will I tell you'
ten_worst.why: The CLAUDE.md test for a steelman is recited as a promise to the room.
ten_worst.replacement: I want to state both cases the way their own defenders would, and only then tell you where I land and why it matters far less for our fellowship than the volume of the argument would suggest.
ten_worst.pattern: P3 rulebook leakage (the prose describing its own method)

ten_worst.quote: So here is the verdict, and the leader must hold it cleanly all the way through the study.
ten_worst.tell: Rulebook word 'verdict' plus a stage direction to the leader inside the teaching
ten_worst.why: The teaching is meant to be James talking. Mid-paragraph it turns and instructs the leader. The same sentence sits in alone-in-a-crowded-church and anxiety session 1.
ten_worst.replacement: So here is where this study stands.
ten_worst.pattern: P3 rulebook leakage (the prose describing its own method)

ten_worst.quote: Bell writes this session from the inside, and he says so plainly, because he was raised without a father, and a man should tell you where he is standing before he talks about a thing like this.
ten_worst.tell: Third-person narrator plus biography as credential
ten_worst.why: The teaching field is James speaking, yet a narrator announces what 'Bell' does and why. A human pastor says it once in his own voice and moves on.
ten_worst.replacement: I was raised without a father, and you should know that before I say anything about this.
ten_worst.pattern: P1 third-person "Bell" narrating James's own teaching

ten_worst.quote: He has five sons who will one day stand at his grave, and he writes toward that grave, not around it.
ten_worst.tell: Biography dramatized into a scene; aphoristic closer
ten_worst.why: Takes a confirmed fact (five sons) and builds an imagined graveside on it, then ends on a 'toward, not around' epigram. Only James can decide whether he wants his sons' future grief used as copy.
ten_worst.pattern: P2 biography stamped as a credential

ten_worst.quote: I have stood at gravesides and said the right words and driven home undone.
ten_worst.tell: First-person pastoral memory scripted for a volunteer to read aloud
ten_worst.why: The volunteer leader is handed a pastor's experience to claim as his own. It is untrue in most mouths and sounds scripted.
ten_worst.replacement: Most of us have stood at a graveside with no idea what to say.
ten_worst.pattern: P2 biography stamped as a credential

ten_worst.quote: Because that is the method, and the method is the message. Bell does not stand outside this. He does not exempt himself from the arithmetic called prudence
ten_worst.tell: Rulebook leakage; chiasmus slogan; third-person Bell
ten_worst.why: 'The method is the message' (or 'the mercy') opens the same FAQ answer in thirty-four places. It is a slogan about the editorial method.
ten_worst.replacement: Because the writer does not exempt himself from the arithmetic called prudence
ten_worst.pattern: P3 rulebook leakage (the prose describing its own method)

ten_worst.quote: Be careful and fair here. This is a contested thesis, not a closed verdict.
ten_worst.tell: Self-instruction left in the prose; 'fair' self-certifying; 'verdict'
ten_worst.why: 'Be careful and fair here' is a note to the writer. The next sentence shows the care without it.
ten_worst.pattern: P3 rulebook leakage (the prose describing its own method)

ten_worst.quote: Not guilt, which burns out. Not politics, which corrupts. Memory.
ten_worst.why: 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' in three fragments, followed five lines later by another ('Not because you are good. Because He was').
ten_worst.replacement: Guilt burns out and politics corrupts, but memory holds.
ten_worst.pattern: P6 aphoristic closers and fragment stacks

ten_worst.quote: This is the most honest objection of all and it deserves the most honest answer, which is to grant it almost entirely.
ten_worst.tell: 'Honest' twice in one sentence; announced concession
ten_worst.why: The word appears about 3,350 times (deconstruction 133, witness 122). BRIEF allows one self-certifying use per piece.
ten_worst.replacement: This objection is mostly right, and I'll say so.

for_james: womanhood session 4 says in your voice, 'I land as a complementarian, but a chastened one,' and baptism-and-communion session 2 says where you land on baptism. Your own essay brief says contested second-order questions are left open and your position is not asserted. Do you want these two statements kept, reworded, or removed?

Eleven guides call themselves companions to books by you: Where Your Treasure Is, After Christendom, Alone in a Crowded Church, Consider the Birds, Character Before Competence, Deep Roots, Mishpat, Raising Believers, The Captive Church, The Undivided Life, Believe. The site's book shelf lists three titles (When God Bless America Replaces Thy Kingdom Come, The Monster in the Mirror, Believe). If the other ten are not available to a reader, the tie-in lines should come out.

Your biography (came to faith from atheism, raised without a father, five sons) is on 49 guides, 297 times, mostly as a reason to trust the study. I recommend one first-person sentence in the one session where it bears on the subject and nowhere else. aging-and-legacy also imagines your sons at your grave ('five sons who will one day stand at his grave', 'who will one day bury him') in the summary, primer, facilitator script and invite caption. Only you can say whether that stays.
Three leader primers call you 'a Michigan pastor' / 'a pastor in Michigan' (christian-nationalism, church-and-empire, economic-justice). True, but outside the confirmed biography list. Keep or cut?

grief and lament give the volunteer leader first-person lines to read aloud as their own ('I have stood at gravesides and said the right words and driven home undone', 'I have prayed prayers that got no answer I could see'). Those are your memories, not theirs. If you want them in, they belong in your teaching in your voice.

About 300 bibliography and further-reading notes end 'Leader to confirm specific claims'. That means the citations were never checked. Someone needs to verify each book and what it is said to argue before the note is removed; I did not verify them.

Several case studies tell a specific story as if it happened ('A man whose daughter had died of an overdose told his grief group...', skeptic's 'a quiet woman named Helen'). The six newer guides frame theirs as 'Suppose...'. If the older ones are composites, they should say 'Suppose' too; if any are real, they need permission and disguise.

grief, lament, suffering, aging-and-legacy and anxiety speak of despair or 'not wanting to live' and point to 'real help' or 'a crisis line' without the 988 number. deconstruction, the-church and marriage discuss abuse without the line that abuse by a church leader should be reported to the authorities. I gave exact fixes for grief and deconstruction; the rest need the same line added.

Your saved Substack profile and VOICE-JAMES-BELL.md disagree in three places, and I followed VOICE-JAMES-BELL.md: the profile wants 2 to 4 sentence paragraphs and 'stacked landing lines' (the standard wants developed paragraphs and warns against one-sentence stacks); the profile wants a 'memorable line the reader screenshots' in every piece (the standard wants one earned verdict, not several attempted slogans, and the quote cards show what the first rule produces at scale); and the profile bans exclamation marks 'ever' and em-dashes only in social writing (the site allows exclamation points inside quoted Scripture and bans em-dashes everywhere).

The sixty-two older guides share one skeleton so closely that sentence fixes will not make them sound like a person. The six newer guides already do. The real decision is whether to rewrite the older sixty-two to that model a few at a time (starting with the crisis-facing ones) or to shelve the weakest until they are rewritten.
strengths: No em-dashes anywhere, no exclamation point outside quoted Scripture, and the Forbidden Language list is effectively clean across 1.6 million words.
Political criticism runs both ways with the same instrument (christian-nationalism, the-captive-church, mishpat, economic-justice each name right and left).
The six newer guides are in the mature register and could sit beside the approved essays.
Real exegetical content under the tics: the 'therefore' linking Matthew 6:24 and 6:25 in money, Elijah fed before he is spoken to in mental-health, the order of Ephesians 5 in marriage.
The crisis lines in mental-health, pastoral-health, youth-who-am-i, when-our-parents-grow-old and addiction-and-recovery are plain and correct.
Leader primers often open with a concrete, observed hazard of the room (money: 'People in a money group do not go silent. They deflect.'), the most human writing in the older guides.
